tagline: Venezuela's lake city and oil capital, split from its opposite shore by a single congested bridge across the strait.
summary: Maracaibo is Venezuela's second city and the heart of its oil industry, set on the western shore of the strait that joins Lake Maracaibo — South America's largest lake — to the Gulf of Venezuela. The lake's eastern shore holds the oil towns of Cabimas and Ciudad Ojeda, connected to Maracaibo today only by the General Rafael Urdaneta Bridge, an ~8.7 km span that carries heavy, congested traffic. The wide, sheltered lake is a natural corridor for a cross-water passenger service that the single bridge cannot fully serve.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Ideal for the cross-lake link to Cabimas (~18nm) and the lakefront hops, all inside Pioneer range, where the tideless, sheltered lake and a heavily congested single bridge make a fast, clean water tier compelling.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for any longer runs down the lake toward the southern shore, where range matters more than frequency.

transit_planning: Cross-lake movement depends entirely on the single Rafael Urdaneta bridge, which is heavily congested; there is no scheduled passenger-vessel alternative, leaving a strong opening for a water tier on a wide, sheltered lake.

competitive_landscape: Cross-lake movement is funnelled entirely onto the congested Rafael Urdaneta bridge with no scheduled passenger-vessel alternative; a clean water tier on the tideless, sheltered lake opens a genuinely new mode. Operating context is shaped by Venezuela's economic and sanctions environment.
seasonality: The Maracaibo basin is hot year-round; the sheltered lake supports operation in all seasons, with the famous Catatumbo lightning storms concentrated over the southern lake and calmer conditions at the northern strait near the city.
regulatory_note: Maritime and lake navigation fall under Venezuela's national aquatic-and-port authority (INEA); passenger-vessel licensing, lake navigation rules and the prevailing sanctions/political-risk context frame any scheduled service.

precedents.why_it_matters: A congested single crossing over a wide lake is the archetypal case for a parallel scheduled water link.
Shows durable industrial willingness-to-pay for fast, reliable cross-lake transfer.
